project: PRD-268 W1 Check-ins: Proactive Auto's engine. Read-only check-ins that suggest, the lane, streaks, Start/Hide, switches and caps, status words, readiness (one branch, one PR, one CI run)
description: PRD-268 (docs/PRDS/PRD-268-PROACTIVE-AUTO.md) wave W1: US-C01–C07, US-C17 and US-C18, re-cut into 19 one-session stories in dependency order. Core only (no frontend); ONE Alembic revision (prd268_w1_proactive); no new dependency; no third-party client. Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd268w1.sh --print-base`.
decisions: K1 Branch and PR. All work happens on feat/prd-268-w1-check-ins in <workspace>/.worktrees/automatos-ai/feat+prd-268-w1-check-ins. The branch is cut from RALPH_BASE_REF: origin/main once PR #1362 (the PRD) has merged, else origin/docs/prd-268-proactive-auto. One PR for the wave (base main, closes tracking issue #1358) and one CI run at the end.
K2 Story order is the dependency order (the `priority` field), and each story gets one session. A story never waits on CI.

K3 Files over 800 lines never grow. Where a story must add lines to one, it moves at least as many lines out in the same commit, to a new module, re-exported when tests import it. Before moving a name, grep orchestrator/tests for `<module>.<name>` patch targets; a name a test patches by module path stays put. The files: services/heartbeat_service.py 1825, modules/tools/discovery/platform_executor.py 1543, modules/tools/execution/unified_executor.py 1390, main.py 1666, modules/agents/factory/agent_factory.py 1982, api/missions.py 2107, api/board_tasks.py 2282, services/activity_service.py 1267, core/llm/manager.py 1063. Re-measure each. The exceptions: orchestrator/config.py gains its settings lines, and route-manifest.json and config-surface.json gain their entries.

K4 Never touch a line inside a function over 50 code lines (scripts/ci/check_changed_code_shape.py fails every touched line inside one). The seams that don't count: a decorator line above `def` (PlatformActionExecutor.clear already has one), a new short function, a new module, a line in a short function (schedule_agent_heartbeat and schedule_orchestrator_heartbeat are short). The gate compares these functions byte for byte with the base: HeartbeatService._agent_tick, _orchestrator_tick, _orchestrator_tick_llm, _dispatch_heartbeat_notification, _route_heartbeat_to_auto, PlatformActionExecutor.clear and PlatformActionExecutor._run_cleared.

K5 This Mac cannot import the orchestrator. route-manifest.json and config-surface.json are edited by hand or with a stdlib-only python snippet, in the format of scripts/dump_routes.py: routes sorted by (path, method), route_count equal to the number of routes, written as json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True) + newline. Setting names go in sorted position.

K6 Exactly one Alembic revision, prd268_w1_proactive, chained onto the current head (re-read EXPECTED_HEAD in orchestrator/tests/test_prd209_alembic_single_head.py; it was prd266_w2_push on 28 Oct). It uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and moves both pins: test_prd209_alembic_single_head.py (the comment chain plus EXPECTED_HEAD) and test_prd236_w1_routes.py (read the new file, assert its down_revision, update the EXPECTED_HEAD line).

K7 Rollout. The proactive mode is off | shadow | live: a platform system setting (category `proactive`, key `mode`), read strictly, with config PROACTIVE_MODE_DEFAULT='off'. A failed read means off, like Socials (modules/socials/settings.py:108-133). In shadow, today's heartbeats run unchanged and check-ins run beside them, recording suggestions. In live, check_in agents and the orchestrator heartbeat at proactive_level silent or notify run check-ins INSTEAD of today's tick. W1 ships no delivery (W2 brings it), so live stays off until W2; the code supports it now and the tests cover it.

K8 The check-in runner owns its tool loop; it never goes through AgentFactory. It offers only read platform actions plus platform_suggest_next_step, and runs every call through PlatformActionExecutor.execute with caller_context lane='check_in', the run id and the run's read log. Composio, plugins, the Anthropic memory tool, sub-agents, Missions and platform_execute are never offered. A decorator on PlatformActionExecutor.clear refuses any call in the lane that isn't positively `read`, unknown actions included (defence in depth). A decorator on UnifiedToolExecutor.execute_tool refuses any non-platform tool in the lane.

K9 Model and caps. Every check-in calls LLMManager(service_name='heartbeat'), the platform orchestrator_llm system setting (default claude-haiku-5-5). An agent's own model_config is not used in the check-in lane. Per run: at most 4 tool iterations, 800 output tokens, 12,000 tokens of context and $0.05; past the ceiling the run stops and records `error`.

K10 Heartbeat mode. heartbeat.mode is check_in | act. When unset: act if the heartbeat's auto_act is true, else check_in (PRD §12-Q1). An agent whose work needs connector reads (Composio) can't do them in a check-in, which fails closed; its owner keeps it `act`. CLI-agent heartbeats (file_cli_ticket, one open per agent) are unchanged in W1. The Run-now routes (run_agent_heartbeat, run_orchestrator_heartbeat) keep today's tick.
K11 The addressee of a suggestion is the workspace owner (§12-Q2).

K12 Start kinds in W1: board_task and chat. The schema accepts mission and playbook_run, but Start answers 409 'not available in this version' for them until US-C14 (W4), where check-ins first propose them. W1's check-in prompts propose board_task or chat only.

K13 Language. Server-written copy (next_step sentences, run notes, refusal text) comes from strings tables in English and Portuguese (Brazil), chosen by the request's Accept-Language (en default). No stored preference in W1. Background copy uses en.

K14 Spend. The lane string 'check_in' joins BACKGROUND_LANES (services/credits/asks.py:38), so a trial never pays for it. background_allowed (services/credits/routing.py:170) and daily_spend_guard.refuse_new_work are checked at every run start. The ceiling is off (0) by default and fails open, so tests set one.

K15 Audit. AuditService.log commits the caller's session (core/workspaces/audit.py:97). Call it after the atomic status UPDATE has committed, or in its own session; never inside the Start or Hide transaction.

K16 Approvals. Gerard approved PRD-268 on 28 Oct 2026 ("get it all started"; tracking issue #1358). This wave adds a guardrail (the lane), changes heartbeat behaviour in live mode and governs background spend: build exactly what the ACs say.

K17 Mislabelled actions. Every action states its level. platform_field_inject writes (handlers_field.py:119) and becomes `write`, with its hierarchy-gate entry (scripts/check_hierarchy_gate.py: _HIERARCHY_TARGETS, admin_only, or ALLOW_LIST with a reason). A read action the sweep catches writing is relabelled, never excepted.
ownerTest: Shadow week, step 0 (PRD §10): set the platform system setting proactive.mode = shadow, then settings.proactive.enabled = true on Gerard's workspace and c1 (PUT /api/proactive/settings). Over the week compare GET /api/proactive/runs with the tickets the heartbeats filed. Live stays off until W2 delivers.
Read 20 random proactive_runs rows: silent runs have zero llm_usage rows; suggested runs cite reads the run made.
Confirm the read-only lane on SaaS: a check-in transcript shows no write tool offered (the run's tool list), and the lane refusal never fired against a legitimate read.

userStories.title: A sweep test: every read action writes nothing
userStories.description: As an owner, I need proof that 'read' means read, so the lane cannot be bypassed by a mislabelled action (PRD-268 §6.2.3, §9).
acceptanceCriteria: New test orchestrator/tests/test_prd268_read_actions_write_nothing.py calls every registered read action's handler with parameters synthesised from its JSON schema (required fields with minimal valid values), against a session whose add, delete, flush, commit and execute of INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE are recorded, and an outbound HTTP transport (httpx and requests) that records; it asserts zero writes per action and names each action that wrote. A handler that raises still counts as checked. → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd268_read_actions_write_nothing.py (new, 15 test functions, 51 cases with the parametrised ones) with its spies in orchestrator/tests/helpers_write_spies.py (new). test_every_read_action_writes_nothing calls each registered read action's PLATFORM_HANDLERS handler (wrappers included) with minimal_params of its schema (required fields only: string '1', enum's first, minimum or 1, False, [] or minItems copies, nested required objects). Each call runs against spy_session (MagicMock(spec=Session) over an empty database; records add, add_all, delete, merge, flush, commit, bulk_*, Query.update/delete, and execute/scalar/scalars of INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, DDL, pg_notify, nextval, on the session, its connection and its engine) and under recording_http (httpx.HTTPTransport.handle_request, httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport.handle_async_request and requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter.send patched to record and answer 200 {}). It asserts zero writes and names each action that wrote with what it wrote and how it ended. A handler that raises or passes 5 s counts as checked; tasks it leaves running are waited for and counted as its own. test_every_read_action_the_sweep_does_not_call_is_refused_in_a_check_in proves the 3 handler-less reads (workspace_read_file, workspace_list_dir, workspace_grep) are not platform actions and never offered. 11 self-tests prove each kind of write is seen, reads are not, a raise or time-out is checked, and the sweep names a mislabelled action. Judgement call (the smaller change), for the owner: the platform's own vector store (config.QDRANT_URL, default http://localhost:6333) is classed as a datastore like Postgres, so only requests that change it are recorded (PUT, DELETE, POST to points/delete, points/payload, snapshots); its reads (GET, retrieve, search, query, scroll, count, facet) are not, and every other HTTP request counts. The PRD's literal 'no outbound HTTP' would also catch, and relabel, platform_search_memory, platform_browse_memories, platform_get_memory_stats, platform_resume_context and platform_get_system_health, which only read the store. Limits, stated in the module docstrings: an empty database hides writes reached only when rows exist; a session the handler opens itself, Redis and boto3 are not watched. code-reviewer: fixed the requests answer under with/stream, wider Query/Result chaining, DDL, pg_notify and nextval as writes, cancelled leftovers awaited, facet a read, exclusiveMinimum/maximum. Not run locally; CI runs it at the end of the wave; commit cd982d4b2

Any read action the sweep catches writing is relabelled write (with its hierarchy-gate status) in the same story, never excepted (K17) → DONE — the sweep catches one read writing, platform_field_query: with the store answering {} it creates the shared field's collection (vector store PUT /collections/...), and on a hit it reinforces every pattern it returns (Hebbian record_access, adapters/vector_field.py _reinforce_batch). It is relabelled write in modules/tools/discovery/actions_field.py and added to ALLOW_LIST with its reason in scripts/check_hierarchy_gate.py (gate OK: 102 writes). Same knock-ons platform_field_inject took in US-C02a: the policy plane classes it internal_write (Strict asks first), it counts toward the platform_write rate limit, receipts count it as a change, and it leaves the check-in surface. Tests: test_what_the_sweep_caught_is_a_write_the_hierarchy_gate_accounts_for, test_what_the_sweep_caught_is_never_offered_or_run_in_a_check_in; test_prd268_action_levels.py's two field_query pins moved to write (is_read now checks platform_field_stability). Static audit of all 114 read handlers (five read-only traces): nothing else is caught under the sweep. Open for the owner, not relabelled because the empty-database sweep cannot reach them: platform_codegraph_get_symbol and platform_codegraph_search INSERT a codegraph_query_logs row and commit the handler's own session on a hit (codegraph_service.py _log_query); platform_search_packages stamps the onboarding funnel and commits when a package matches; platform_query_data writes audit and training rows when a source exists; platform_read_document writes CSV copies of a spreadsheet to the workspace; platform_search_documents inserts telemetry and updates last_accessed through its own sessions; platform_get_system_health (super-admin only) sets a Redis probe key. Contrary to the note in US-C02c, platform_web_fetch and platform_web_search are not caught (url '1' fails URL checks before any request, and CI has no search backend), so they stay read and are offered in check-ins: an outbound-fetch channel a prompt-injected check-in could use. Relabelling them write is the owner's call (Strict would then ask before web reads in chat). Also outside the tool lane: ContextMode.CHECK_IN's field_memory section calls query_workspace with record_access left True, so building a check-in's context reinforces the field. Commit cd982d4b2

No new dependency (use unittest.mock and the existing fixtures) → DONE — no dependency added: no requirements file changed; the spies use unittest.mock (MagicMock, patch) and libraries the orchestrator already pins (sqlalchemy 2.0.23, httpx 0.28.1, requests 2.34.2 in requirements.lock); no new fixture or conftest change; commit cd982d4b2
userStories.notes: Registry: get_action_registry().get_by_permission('read') (action_registry.py:166-169). Handlers: PLATFORM_HANDLERS (platform_executor.py:1277). Keep the test file at most 800 lines; helpers may go in a tests helper module.

subject_key helpers (agent error streak 'agent:<id>:error:<class>', ticket 'ticket:<number>', title 'title:<normalised>'); is_duplicate(candidate, open_rows, hidden_rows, now) with the 14-day hidden window; acceptanceCriteria: services/readiness/ with one probe per server item: core (SELECT 1), model_route (the orchestrator_llm setting resolves to a configured provider and model, no model call), web_search (a search provider is configured), push (the Expo push path or operator consent is configured); each with a timeout from config (READINESS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) where a timeout reads not_checked; items carry needed_by and a fix href that is an app path
GET /api/readiness and POST /api/readiness/check (rate-limited with the existing limiter), authenticated and workspace-scoped, plain def; in the route manifest
On SaaS no detail contains a hostname or latency; the local edition may show them
New test orchestrator/tests/test_prd268_readiness.py: each probe's three states; a timeout gives not_checked; fix hrefs start with '/'; no hostname on saas; the rate limit
userStories.notes: Reuse api/system_health_checks.py _database where possible (it has no timeout: wrap it). No calendar item in W1 (§12-Q20).

instructions: Mark an AC done by appending, outside backticks and exactly as written, `→ DONE — <evidence>`. An AC only the owner can check gets `→ OWNER: <what to check>`.
